claims: Every ELIGIBLE or INTEGRATED candidate, selected or unselected, enters generic authority-aware history validation.
Candidate authority is the latest non-superseded ACTIVE workstream entry, not a later COMPLETE entry or a superseded activation.
The trusted entry-introducing commit must be an ancestor of or equal to candidate.base_commit; copying exact entry bytes onto a stale branch does not satisfy ancestry.
A bootstrap candidate may predate its authority entry only when the trusted entry-introducing commit is exactly the first commit in its validated linear candidate range.
Fourteen ordinary existing candidates satisfy the ancestry floor and the historical CC-000 candidate satisfies only the structural bootstrap allowance.
Quiet Bell candidate remains NONE, all content paths remain absent, and the Small Shop process-only and three-control execution boundaries are unchanged.
limitations: This fact verifies repository governance admission only. It creates no oracle content, candidate, compiler semantic, runtime, package, release, selection, or public contract.
OVR-000240 must be committed before it can become the trusted floor for future Quiet Bell candidate admission.

summary: Verify generic trusted-history candidate authority admission.
why: The hardening report and OVR-000238 mechanically distinguish trusted Git ancestry from copied governance bytes, admit descendant bases, cover unselected candidates, preserve existing candidate compatibility, and keep every content and downstream boundary unchanged.
